Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Pakistan's reply. It is all smiles in the Scottish huddle and understandably so. The two umpires lead the way, followed by the two openers of Pakistan, Muneeba Ali and Gull Feroza. Scotland are starting with spin in the form of Katherine Fraser. Feroza to face the first ball. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Disciplined bowling undone by poor fielding - Pakistan's bowling attack showed glimpses of control and bowled well in short patches to pick up periodic wickets. However, their hard work was completely undone by a horrific display on the field, marred by dropped catches and misfields. The Asian side now faces a mountain to climb, needing a massive 192 runs to secure a victory and head into the Women's T20 World Cup with winning momentum.

Bryce's masterclass - The momentum shifted dramatically after the Powerplay when Katherine Fraser departed, bringing Kathryn Bryce to the crease. Pakistan had a golden opportunity to derail the Scottish innings early, but they grassed a crucial catch when Kathryn was on just 6. This proved to be the turning point of the Scotland innings, as the Scottish captain never looked back, ticking the scoreboard over at a rapid clip despite losing a few partners at the other end. As the death overs approached, Kathryn Bryce shifted gears into absolute overdrive with a breathtaking display of power hitting. She completely dismantled the opposition bowling in the final two overs, smashing six boundaries and a towering six to finish on a magnificent 94.

Cautious start lays the foundation - Scotland Women began their innings with a measured and disciplined approach after being invited to bat first. Thanks to fireworks from Kathryn Bryce, Scotland have posted a formidable total of 191 for 5 on the board at the end of their 20 overs. The Scottish openers focused on keeping wickets intact, navigating the early movement to score 41 runs in the Powerplay without shedding a single wicket. This risk-free, stable opening partnership provided the ideal launchpad, setting a perfect foundation for the middle order to play freely and attack later in the innings.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to commence. Fatima Sana and her troops disperse from the huddle and take the field. Darcey Carter and Katherine Fraser are the two Scottish openers. Fatima Sana has the new ball in her hand. A slip in place for Carter. Off we go...

PITCH REPORT - Shachi Pai is down by the pitch, and she informs that nearly 80 overs of cricket have been played so far on this used surface. There is still a bit of grass on offer, which should aid seam movement early on, while the fact that it is a previously used pitch means the spinners are also expected to come into play as the game progresses. With the weather around, Pai feels it is a no-brainer to bowl first. Shares that there is also a lovely cross breeze blowing across the ground, something the seamers will look to make use of. As for a score, she believes 150 could be around par on this wicket.

The skipper of Scotland Women - Kathryn Bryce says they were anyway looking to bat first, feeling that this used surface is likely to become trickier to bat on as the day progresses. Mentions that they will take the field with an aim to win. Feels when you go out and win games, it gives you confidence heading into the main tournament. Bryce shares that the weather here in Cardiff is pretty similar to what they are used to back home in Scotland.

The captain of Pakistan Women - Fatima Sana says that they will be bowling first as they want to try bowling first ahead of the World Cup. She mentions that they just need to be a bit more clinical with the ball and in the field. Sana informs that they are going in with the full squad of 15, but will probably give some players a chance.

Pakistan Women - Muneeba Ali (WK), Gull Feroza, Ayesha Zafar, Natalia Pervaiz, Saira Jabeen, Eyman Fatima, Fatima Sana (C), Aliya Riaz, Iram Javed, Tuba Hassan, Rameen Shamim, Sadia Iqbal, Nashra Sundhu, Diana Baig and Tasmia Rubab.

Scotland Women - Darcey Carter, Katherine Fraser, Kathryn Bryce (C), Sarah Bryce (WK), Megan McColl, Priyanaz Chatterji, Rachel Slater, Kirstie Gordon, Chloe Abel, Abtaha Maqsood, Gabriella Fontenla, Ailsa Lister, Maisie Maceira, Olivia Bell and Pippa Sproul.
TOSS - The sun is out, and we are all set for the flip of the coin. The coin goes up and comes down in favour of Fatima Sana. Pakistan Women elect to BOWL first.

What to expect? This warm-up is less about experimentation and more about execution, with both Scotland and Pakistan already familiar with conditions in Derby. Scotland carry early momentum after a strong, well-rounded performance in their opening game, while Pakistan will be aiming to fix inconsistencies and find more control across both innings after a disappointing start. There was a bit of rain around the previous day of warm-ups, but two full games were still completed, and the forecast looks much better this time, which is good news for another uninterrupted run-out as both sides fine-tune ahead of the World Cup.

Pakistan's power without control - The Asian side carries more individual match-winners on paper, with Fatima Sana standing out as a genuine all-round threat who can contribute in both powerplay and death overs. Muneeba Ali and Gull Feroza provide stability at the top, but the team's main challenge has been converting starts into dominant totals, with middle-order collapses often halting momentum. Their bowling attack has wicket-taking options, but control in the middle overs and death overs remains a concern. When under pressure, Pakistan have struggled to maintain lengths and build sustained pressure, something they will need to address against a solid Scotland batting unit. Players like Sadia Iqbal and Rameen Shamim will be key in controlling the tempo through spin.

Balanced core leading the way - Scotland's biggest strength lies in their balance across departments, with a batting line-up that has shown the ability to rotate strike and build partnerships through players like Kathryn Bryce, Darcey Carter and Priyanaz Chatterji. Bryce, in particular, remains the key engine of this side, capable of anchoring innings while also accelerating when needed. Katherine Fraser provides control and wickets in the middle overs, supported well by Abtaha Maqsood's spin variations and Gabriella Fontenla's disciplined lines. However, Scotland's batting can still be tested against higher-quality pace attacks, especially if early wickets fall and the middle order is exposed under pressure. Their dependency on a few core performers also remains a factor, meaning consistency from the top order will be crucial against stronger opposition.

Momentum check in Derby - Greetings, all. Scotland Women and Pakistan Women face off in Derby in their second ICC Women's World Cup 2026 warm-up fixture, with both sides using this fixture as a key checkpoint before the main tournament. Scotland enter with growing confidence after a strong all-round showing in their previous outing, while Pakistan will be aiming to correct course after a below-par performance, making this a clash between a settled unit and a side still searching for rhythm.
